Name: Easy Access Buttons
Author: yadm18
Description:
[heading]One column for every inventory button[/heading]

Mods that add an inventory button all aim for the same spot beside the bag, so the buttons cover each other. Easy Access Buttons gives them one shared column on the right edge of the inventory page.

The column already includes the Community Center button and Organize. Extra buttons fill that column downward, then a second column, then a third. When there are more buttons than fit, the arrows under the column scroll them. The [b]...[/b] button under the column opens a menu where you reorder or hide any button. The trash can stays under the first column.

This mod works on its own. With no other mods installed, the column is the Community Center button, Organize, and the gear.

[list]
[*]Stardew Valley 1.6.14 or later[/*]
[*]SMAPI 4.1.0 or later[/*]
[/list]
[heading]Mods that join the column on their own[/heading]

These mods call the API. Install Easy Access Buttons and their button lines up with the others. Leave Easy Access Buttons out, and each one keeps the button it had before.

[line]
[size=4][b][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/53287]Perfection Shortcut[/url][/b][/size]
by Yadm

After Qi's Walnut Room unlocks, the inventory button opens the game's perfection tracker. It joins this column when Easy Access Buttons is installed.
[line]
[size=4][b][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/53092]Guild Kill List[/url][/b][/size]
by Yadm

After you reach floor 100 of the Mines, Marlon writes. Visit the guild and the monster eradication list is added to your inventory. That button joins this column when Easy Access Buttons is installed.
[line]

[heading]Mods moved by an optional file on this page[/heading]

These mods do not call the API. Each one still draws its own button, and an optional file on this page moves that button into the column. Download a patch only for a mod you use. The main Easy Access Buttons file does not need any of them, and none of these patches are required for each other.

[line]
[size=4][b][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/10384]Convenient Inventory[/url][/b][/size]
by gaussfire

Quick Stack to Nearby Chests moves into the column. Install the optional file [b]Easy Access Buttons for Convenient Inventory[/b]. The hotkey still quick-stacks when the button is hidden or scrolled off. Chest menus stay where Convenient Inventory put them.
[line]
[size=4][b][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/17265]Unlockable Bundles[/url][/b][/size]
by DeLiXx

The Bundle Overview button moves into the column. Install the optional file [b]Easy Access Buttons for Unlockable Bundles[/b]. Unlockable Bundles still draws the icon, handles the click, and shows its hover tip.
[line]
[size=4][b][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/43127]UI Info Suite 2 Alternative[/url][/b][/size]
by DazUki

The calendar, billboard, special orders, and Qi's special orders icons move into the column, each on the same button background as the other buttons. Install the optional file [b]Easy Access Buttons for UI Info Suite 2 Alternative[/b]. This is for DazUki's Alternative. Annosz's original UI Info Suite 2 is a different mod, and this file does not change it. The keybinds still open those boards when an icon is hidden or scrolled off. The bookseller and Robin icons stay on the HUD.
[line]

[heading]For mod authors[/heading]

Your mod does not reference Easy Access Buttons.dll. Copy the interface below into your own project. The interface must be public, and it must not be nested inside another class. On [b]GameLaunched[/b], ask SMAPI for it:

[code]
var api = this.Helper.ModRegistry.GetApi<IEasyAccessButtonsApi>("Yadm.EasyAccessButtons");
if (api is null)
    return;[/code]
Null means this mod is not installed. There are two ways to list the dependency.

Use [b]IsRequired true[/b] when your button only makes sense in the column. SMAPI will not load your mod without Easy Access Buttons.

[code]
"Dependencies": [
  { "UniqueID": "Yadm.EasyAccessButtons", "IsRequired": true }
][/code]
Use [b]IsRequired false[/b] when your mod should still load on its own. Keep your old button when [b]GetApi[/b] returns null.

[code]
"Dependencies": [
  { "UniqueID": "Yadm.EasyAccessButtons", "IsRequired": false }
][/code]
[heading]Add a button this mod draws[/heading]

[b]AddButton[/b] registers a button. Easy Access Buttons draws it, shows the tooltip, plays the select sound, and runs your click. The same id replaces the previous registration. An empty id is ignored.

[code]
public interface IEasyAccessButtonsApi
{
    void AddButton(string id, int order, Texture2D texture, Rectangle sourceRect, int iconSize, Func<bool> isVisible, Func<string> tooltip, Action onClick);
    void RemoveButton(string id);
    void Reserve(string id, int order, Func<bool> isVisible);
    void Reserve(string id, int order, Func<bool> isVisible, Func<string> name, Texture2D? icon, Rectangle sourceRect);
    Rectangle GetBounds(string id);
}[/code]
[code]
api.AddButton(
    id: "tracker",
    order: 0,
    texture: Game1.mouseCursors,
    sourceRect: new Rectangle(346, 400, 8, 8),
    iconSize: 32,
    isVisible: () => this.Config.Enabled,
    tooltip: () => this.Helper.Translation.Get("button.tooltip"),
    onClick: this.OpenTracker);[/code]
[list]
[*][b]id[/b] is unique inside your mod. It is stored as your UniqueID, a slash, and that id.[/*]
[*][b]order[/b]: a lower number sits higher until the player rearranges the list. The same number is sorted by id. The Community Center button and Organize use lower numbers than a normal mod button, so yours starts under them.[/*]
[*][b]iconSize[/b] is the icon in pixels inside the 64-pixel cell.[/*]
[*][b]isVisible[/b] is checked every layout. False removes the button from the column and closes the gap. The row stays in the gear menu, greyed, with a note that your mod is hiding it.[/*]
[*][b]tooltip[/b] is the hover text. Empty draws no tooltip.[/*]
[*][b]onClick[/b] runs after the select sound, while the inventory menu is still open. Do not play that sound again. A click with an item on the cursor is left for the game.[/*]
[*]To open another menu, close the inventory menu and open the next menu on the following tick.[/*]
[*]The player's saved order is kept. A button this mod has not seen before is added at the end of that list until the player moves it. Reset in the gear menu clears the saved list.[/*]
[*][b]RemoveButton[/b] drops a button you added or reserved.[/*]
[/list]
[heading]Move a button your mod still draws[/heading]

Use this when your mod already has an inventory button and should keep drawing, clicking, and showing its own tooltip. [b]Reserve[/b] claims a cell. Easy Access Buttons does not draw that icon. The longer [b]Reserve[/b] also supplies the gear-menu name and icon. An empty source rectangle uses the whole texture.

After the inventory page lays out, [b]GetBounds[/b] returns that cell. It returns an empty rectangle when the button is hidden, scrolled off, or the page has not been laid out yet. Write that rectangle onto your own widget. Use the same id you passed to [b]Reserve[/b]. When the rectangle is empty, park the widget off the page so it is not left on its old spot. Do not draw the icon a second time.

[code]
api.Reserve(
    id: "overview",
    order: 30,
    isVisible: () => true,
    name: () => "Bundle Overview",
    icon: this.Icon,
    sourceRect: new Rectangle(0, 0, 61, 56));

Rectangle cell = api.GetBounds("overview");[/code]

Downloads.Description: Main file for Easy Access Buttons 1.0.0. Lines inventory buttons up in one column beside the bag, and a gear menu reorders or hides them. Unzip into Stardew Valley/Mods, or install the zip with Vortex. Requires Stardew Valley 1.6.14+ and SMAPI 4.1.0+.
